prompt_name: Margazhi Kolam in a Thanjavur Courtyard

subject.description: An adult kolam artist drawing a precise pulli kolam with rice flour at the household threshold
subject.textile: Thirubuvanam silk saree with a deep arakku-red body, muted mustard-gold korvai border, and restrained rudraksha-inspired motifs
subject.festival: Margazhi observance before sunrise, with one brass kuthuvilakku and a small plate of fresh jasmine and arali flowers

setting.place: an inhabited courtyard house near the old residential streets of Thanjavur
setting.period: present day, preserving a late-19th-century Tamil domestic setting
setting.architecture: lime-plastered courtyard house with red-oxide floors, Burmese-teak pillars, carved wooden doors, a shaded thinnai, inner mutram, and weathered clay roof tiles

time_of_day: blue hour before sunrise on a cool Margazhi morning

lighting.description: soft dawn-blue ambient light mixed with a restrained warm glow from one brass oil lamp

camera.composition: artist and kolam slightly off-centre, with pillars creating depth and an uncluttered lived-in courtyard
camera.focus: the drawing hand and emerging rice-flour line are clear while the architecture remains readable

style: photorealistic documentary cinema; culturally precise, quiet, inhabited, and unstaged rather than picturesque or postcard-like

motion.subject_motion: the artist pinches and releases rice flour in a continuous line, completes one loop of the pulli kolam, briefly adjusts the saree edge, then resumes drawing
motion.environment_motion: the oil-lamp flame flickers subtly while jasmine strands and nearby leaves move slightly in the dawn breeze
motion.camera_move: a slow stabilized 20-centimetre push-in with no orbit or sudden reframing
motion.start_frame: medium-wide view showing the artist, threshold, and half-completed kolam
motion.end_frame: slightly tighter view emphasizing the moving hand, rice-flour line, and red-oxide floor
motion.continuity: preserve the same person, saree, jewellery, kolam geometry, lamp position, architecture, and lighting throughout

avoid: North Indian clothing or festival props
changing face or clothing between frames
